title: "Hive on Start + Void"
description: "Cutover packet for the native Hive Worker: names, bindings, build, smoke checks and rollback."
updatedAt: "2026-11-10"
audience: developers
---

`apps/hive` has native TanStack Start + Vite+ + Void source beside its Next build,
generated by the [start-bridge codemod](/build/devops/start-bridge-codemod). The Next
build and `vercel.json` are untouched. `hive.tuturuuu.com` serves the maintenance
Worker below until a release owner flips the route. That 503 is the approved
interim response, not a failed native deploy.

## Maintenance Worker and the native Worker

Flipping `hive.tuturuuu.com` between these Workers is a product decision for the
release owner. It is not a build defect, and this packet does not perform the flip.

| | Maintenance | Native Start Worker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Script | `tuturuuu-hive-maintenance` | `tuturuuu-hive` when `VITE_HIVE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production`; `tuturuuu-hive-vite-staging` otherwise |
| Module | `apps/hive/maintenance/worker.mjs` | `apps/hive/cloudflare/worker.ts`, emitted into `dist` |
| Config that deploys it | `apps/hive/maintenance/metadata.json` (Workers script upload metadata: `main_module` `worker.mjs`, compatibility date `2026-10-26`, empty `bindings`). There is no Wrangler file for this page. | Wrangler config emitted by `apps/hive/void.config.ts` (`dist/server/wrangler.json` through the deploy pointer). The config attaches no route. |
| Route | Zone route `hive.tuturuuu.com/*` bound to `tuturuuu-hive-maintenance`. DNS stays a proxied discard record, so the Worker answers the host and does not fall through to the old tunnel origin. | None until cutover. |

The maintenance module returns HTTP 503, `Retry-After: 300`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, and `noindex` for every path, including API and WebSocket upgrades. It has no bindings and no upstream calls.

A cutover to the native Worker replaces the script on the existing route `hive.tuturuuu.com/*`: the pattern stays, and the script becomes `tuturuuu-hive`. Leave `tuturuuu-hive-maintenance` uploaded. Rollback points that same route back at `tuturuuu-hive-maintenance`. No database write and no rebuild of the maintenance module is required to put the maintenance page back.

## Worker

- Profile selector: `VITE_HIVE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production` at build time. Staging stays the default (`workers_dev` and `preview_urls` off, `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`). Production is `tuturuuu-hive` with the same route flags and `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=0`. Nothing in config attaches a route.
- Entry: `apps/hive/cloudflare/worker.ts`.
- Host: `hive.tuturuuu.com`. Root-only: `mountHosts` is empty and `unknownHost` is `reject`, so `tuturuuu.com/hive` and any other host answer 404 before app code runs.
- Binding: `ASSETS` (static output, `run_worker_first`). No D1 binding. `apps/hive/db/migrations` is Postgres SQL for `HIVE_DATABASE_URL`. `void.config.ts` sets `database: 'pg'` so Void does not emit those files as a local D1 binding (`DB` / `database_id: local`). The Apps seal still requires `d1_databases` to be the empty normalizer default.
- Variables (names): `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX`, optional `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN` (default `https://tuturuuu.com`).
- Secrets (names, set in the Worker, never in the repo): `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`, `HIVE_DATABASE_URL`, `HIVE_REALTIME_TOKEN_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`, `CRON_SECRET`. Compare with the Vercel project environment list before the flip.
- Optional variables read by the source: `HIVE_REALTIME_URL`, `HIVE_OLLAMA_BASE_URL`, `HIVE_APP_URL`. Realtime ownership is in the [Hive realtime runbook](/build/devops/hive-realtime-runbook).
- Hive talks to its own database and realtime service; confirm both are reachable from Workers before the flip.

## Build and qualification

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun turbo:local run build --filter=@tuturuuu/hive^... --concurrency=2
bun scripts/ci/generate-build-metadata.ts
bun run --cwd apps/hive routes:check
bun run --cwd apps/hive type-check:cloudflare
export VITE_HIVE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production
export HIVE_SOURCE_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
export GITHUB_OUTPUT="$(mktemp)" RUNNER_TEMP="$(mktemp -d)"
bun run --cwd apps/hive build:cloudflare
CI=true CI_SOURCE_SHA="$HIVE_SOURCE_SHA" bun run --cwd apps/hive test:runtime
python3 scripts/ci/hive-native-artifact.py config apps/hive
python3 scripts/ci/hive-native-artifact.py seal apps/hive --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/hive-native-artifact.json"
python3 scripts/ci/hive-native-artifact.py pack apps/hive --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/hive-native-artifact.json" --archive "$RUNNER_TEMP/hive-cutover.tar.gz"
```

`hive-cloudflare.yaml` runs the same production profile in its `hive-cutover-artifact` job and seals the emitted config with `scripts/ci/hive-native-artifact.py`. The seal reads the config Void wrote. It does not rewrite Worker name, vars, or normalized fields after the build. Run the build on a CI or remote runner, not a developer machine.

`test:runtime` starts the emitted Worker in workerd
with synthetic secrets and no network egress: build identity, root host, apex rejection,
unknown paths, and the signed-out redirect through the app-owned
`cloudflare/auth-redirect.runtime.mjs` fixture (8 checks).

The app proxy admits anonymous `GET`/`HEAD /api/build-info` without an app-session
refresh, so deployment verification gets `200` instead of `401`.

## Smoke checks after the route is attached

```bash
curl -sI https://hive.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info   # 200, JSON, no-store
curl -sI https://hive.tuturuuu.com/                 # 307 to /login for a signed-out client
curl -sI https://hive.tuturuuu.com/login            # renders, no 5xx
curl -sI https://tuturuuu.com/hive        # 404 (root-only app)
```

Every page redirects signed-out users to login, so a signed-in check needs a test
session and belongs to the release owner. No smoke request may return `5xx`.

## Rollback

The live origin is the maintenance Worker. After a native cutover, put maintenance
back by binding the route `hive.tuturuuu.com/*` to `tuturuuu-hive-maintenance` again.
Keep the maintenance script in place so rollback is that route change.

1. Before the flip, record the route id, the script it points at (`tuturuuu-hive-maintenance`), and the DNS record for `hive.tuturuuu.com`.
2. To leave maintenance, point `hive.tuturuuu.com/*` at `tuturuuu-hive`. To restore maintenance, point the same pattern back at `tuturuuu-hive-maintenance`.
3. Rerun the maintenance checks (503, `Retry-After: 300`, noindex) or the native smoke checks, matching the script the route names.

Rolling back touches no database rows and no migrations. Route changes belong to the release owner.
